CATAQUIZ City of San Pedro, guna Dear Mayor Cataquiz, DILG Legal Opinion No. 14 S. 2016 26 We write letter requesting this Department's reconsideration of DILG Opinion No. 50, series of 2015, which denied your request for authority to appoint barangay officials of the newly created barangays of San Pedro, Laguna. In your letter, you posit that the appointment of officials and employees of the newly created barangays should emanate from the LCE of San Pedro City, as provided under Section 455 (b)(l)(v) of the Local Government Code (LGC) following its express mandate to provide for the financial requirements of barangays greated by LGUs pursuant to Article 14 (g) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the LGC. You also propose, in the alternative, the establishment of a transition team that will be vested with the proper authority to oversee the current situation of the newly created barangays and prepare the same towards formal constitution and come the next regular election of barangay officials, to ensure that the newly created barangays will be adequately prepared to take on the responsibilities attached to their creation, and the officials to be elected shall be able to assume more efficiently. Please be informed that the Department sustains its earlier opinion/ interpretation of Section 455 (b)(l)(v) of the LGC that the City Mayor's gower to appoint only extends to appointive officials and employees whose appointments are not providedfor by the Code'or by law, i.e., Republic Act No. 10420, otherwise known as' the Charter of the City of San Pedro, as in this case. Note that the Mayor's power to appoint elective barangay officials arises only in case of a permanent vacancy in the sangguniang barangay as expressly provided under Section 45 (a)(3) of the LGC Moreover, there is "vacancy" to speak of as the newly created barangays' corporate existence has yet to begin. 'Anent this Departmeni's 'reliance on Section 14 'of thel LGC, note that it clearly and unambiguously provides when the corporate existence of a local government unit shall commence, i.e., upon the election and qualification of its chief executive and majority of the members of the sanggunian, in the absence of a declaration of the time for its commencement in the law or ordinance creating it.

'It . is a cardinal rule in statutory construction that where the law speaks in clear and categorical language, there is no occasi n for interpretation, there is only room for application.l Hence, the newly creat barangays shall remain tinder the control and supervision of the incumbent elective officials Of Barangay San Vicente, City of San Pedro, pending election and qualification of the respec •ve barangay officials thereof pursuant to Laguna Provincial Ordinance No. 9, s. 1997. As regards lhe establishment of a "transition team," please be advised that the Department finds nothing objectionable ther in for as Ibng as their functions are merely advisory, which shall be limited to aiding you in the performance of your duties as the local chief executive (LCE). Under the LGC, the City Mayor's pow rs and duties include: Section 455. Chief Executive; Powers, Duties and Compensation. (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the city mayor shall: (I) Exercise general supervision land control over all programs, projects, services; and activitieS •of city government. and in this connection, shall: (xiii) Visit component barangays of the city at least once every six (6) months to deepen his understanding of problems and conditions, listen and give appropriate counsel to, local officials and inhabitants, inform the component barangay officials and inhabitants of general laws and ordinances which especially concern 'ther», and otherwise conduct visits and inspections to ensure that the governance of the city will improve the quality of life of the inhabitants; (2) Enforce all laws and ordinances relative to the governance of the city and in the exercise of the appropriate corporate powers provided for under Section 22 of this Code, implement all approved policies, programs, projects, services and activitiös of the city and, in addition to the foregoing, shall: (i) Ensure that the acts of $he city's component barangays and of its officials and employees are within the scope of their prescribed powers, duties and functions; Said "transition team" I may conduct necessary studies or visits to advice' you accordingly for any dispositive action you may take in the exercise of your supervisory powers over your component barangays. Per Section 22 (c ) of the-LGC in relation to Section 455 (b)(l)(vi), the LCE may enter into a contract of service on behalf of the LGU upon prior authorization of the sanggunian concerned. Pertinent sub-items Of Section 261 of the Omnibus Election Code as reiterated .in Comelec Resolution No. 10030, on the other hand, provide the prohibited personnel actions during the election period.
